# SOOS — Distributed Governance Runtime (KEE-2/SOOS-DIST)
# draft-sato-soos-dist-00
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/kee2/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: 30 July 2026

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

KEE-2/SOOS-DIST specifies the Distributed Governance Runtime for the
Sovereign Object OS: the five distributed properties (D1-D5) that enable
SOOS governance to operate at enterprise and national-infrastructure scale
without prohibitive cost. KEE-2 is additive to KEE-1 [draft-sato-soos-
kee-00] — it does not replace any KEE-1 property. It adds Cedar cluster
consensus (D1), FROST signing cluster management (D2), Session Block GAR
with Merkle DAG (D3), catalog distribution protocol (D4), and ACD session
inheritance (D5). KEE-2 compliance is triggered by five quantitative
performance walls; a deployment below all five walls is KEE-1-only
compliant. KEE-2 is not a quality upgrade; it is a scale compliance
requirement.

What KEE-2 is NOT: KEE-2 does not define new SOOS protocol semantics
visible to AEP sessions, PEER transactions, or ACD Records. A KEE-2
kernel is protocol-indistinguishable from a KEE-1 kernel to consumers
of the SOOS protocol layer. The exception is D4, which introduces
ALE-DIST-01 through ALE-DIST-06 to the GAR ALE registry.

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

At KEE-1 scale, SOOS governance produces one cryptographic signing
operation per Audit Log Event. A naively scaled KEE-1 deployment at
national-mandate scale (millions of agent sessions per day, each producing
dozens of ALEs) produces hundreds of millions of signed writes per hour.
This is the SharedSignal fan-out failure pattern: Microsoft's SharedSignal
deployment produced near-data-center failure because security events with
cryptographic signing per event overwhelmed authentication infrastructure
that was correctly sized for ordinary load. SOOS faces the same structural
risk in GAR.

The failure mode is not data center capacity; it is a design problem that
looks like a data center problem. A government that mandates SOOS
compliance must be able to assure regulated operators that compliance cost
is marginal — comparable to existing authentication and audit logging
infrastructure, not net-new data center capacity. KEE-2 Session Block GAR
(D3) reduces signing operations from event-granularity to block-granularity:
approximately two orders of magnitude reduction. Cedar Evaluation Cache (D1)
reduces Cedar evaluation CPU by an estimated 80% at typical workloads. FROST
Signing Cluster (D2) eliminates the single-node signing throughput bottleneck.

The catalog distribution problem (D4) is distinct: without a specified
protocol, each operator implements their own mechanism for propagating
CAP-RRS catalog updates to their kernel fleet. At national-mandate scale,
this produces inconsistent effective-date activation — some kernels
activating a new regulation before its legal date, others activating it
late or not at all. D4 Coordinated Activation solves this with a two-phase
commit protocol: distribute-and-validate (Phase 1), then coordinated-
activate at effective_date (Phase 2).

---

## SECTION 3 — Key Normative Concepts

Deployment Wall / Performance Wall:
   A quantitative scale threshold at which a KEE-1 deployment requires
   the corresponding KEE-2 property. Five walls: W1 (>1,000 Cedar
   eval/sec sustained → D1); W2 (>100 KIA sign/sec sustained → D2);
   W3 (>10,000 ALE writes/sec sustained → D3); W4 (any multi-kernel
   fleet with shared Catalog Authority → D4); W5 (sub-agent delegation
   chains >2 levels at scale → D5). Crossing a wall without implementing
   the corresponding property is a KEE-2 compliance failure.

Cedar Evaluation Cache:
   A deterministic cache of Cedar evaluation results keyed by the
   triple (action_type, context_hash, cap_profile_hash). The cache
   MUST be invalidated in full on any Cedar Policy Set transition.
   Cache entries MUST NOT be used across a cap_profile_hash boundary.

Coordinated Activation:
   The two-phase commit protocol by which all kernels in a fleet
   activate a catalog update atomically at a declared effective_date.
   Phase 1: distribute-and-validate (each kernel receives, validates
   publisher key threshold signature, and acknowledges). Phase 2:
   coordinated-activate (each kernel activates at effective_date).
   A kernel that cannot activate in Phase 2 MUST enter DENY-all mode
   for actions governed by the updated Tier 1 controls.

FROST Signing Cluster:
   A distributed deployment of FROST signer instances each holding
   one key share of the GEC's threshold keypair. FROST threshold
   parameters (t,n) MUST NOT be dynamically reduced during operation.
   Quorum failure (fewer than t live signers) MUST cause signing-
   suspended mode — MUST NOT fall back to single-signer operation.

GAR Session Block:
   The unit of GAR audit storage in KEE-2. Contains all ALEs from
   one agent session as a prev_span_hash chain, with a Merkle root
   over all ALEs and a KIA threshold signature over (block_id,
   Merkle_root, block_close_timestamp). One signing operation per
   block, not per ALE.

Kernel Fleet:
   The set of all KEE-2-compliant kernel instances operated by a
   single operator that share a common Catalog Authority and receive
   the same catalog distribution feed. Fleet membership declared in
   each kernel's GEC Manifest via fleet_id.

Merkle DAG:
   A directed acyclic graph of Merkle trees over GAR Session Blocks.
   Anchor Interval: RECOMMENDED maximum 60 seconds for government-
   tier deployments. Anchor gap >1.5x interval: MUST emit
   soos.gar.anchor_gap_detected OTel event. Anchor gap >3x interval:
   MUST enter CEDAR_DENY-all mode.

XPID Federation Certificate: [NEW in dist-00]
   A signed artifact enabling a remote cluster to verify a presented
   XPID value. Contains: the XPID value, the ptxn_id of the
   originating PEER transaction, the originating GEC's KIA attestation
   chain, and the originating GEC's signature over the tuple
   (xpid, ptxn_id, verifying_cluster_id). A cluster MUST NOT accept
   a raw XPID value without federation certificate verification.

ALE-DIST-01 through ALE-DIST-06: [NEW in dist-00]
   Catalog distribution event types added to the GAR ALE registry.
   ALE-DIST-01: CAP_CATALOG_RECEIVED. ALE-DIST-02: CAP_CATALOG_
   REJECTED_INVALID_PUBLISHER_KEY. ALE-DIST-03: CAP_CATALOG_ROLLBACK_
   BLOCKED. ALE-DIST-04: CAP_CATALOG_ACTIVATED. ALE-DIST-05:
   MERKLE_ANCHOR_PRODUCED. ALE-DIST-06: MERKLE_ANCHOR_GAP_DETECTED.

Tiered GAR Storage:
   Hot tier (in-memory + NVMe, 24h, in agent critical path); Warm
   tier (compressed SSD/Zstandard, 90 days, async); Cold tier (object
   storage encrypted, 7 years per APPI Art.19, async). Only Hot tier
   is in the agent action critical path.

---

## SECTION 4 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

Raft/etcd: KEE-2 D1 adopts Raft consensus via etcd as the Cedar Policy
Set coordination mechanism. KEE-2 profiles Raft with SOOS-specific
failure handling: stale-policy-window timeout (RECOMMENDED 30 seconds),
CEDAR_DENY-all mode on quorum loss, and the soos.governance.cedar.
split_brain OTel event for split-brain detection. KEE-2 does not redefine
Raft safety or liveness properties.

FROST [draft-irtf-cfrg-frost]: KEE-2 D2 REQUIRES FROST as the threshold
signing scheme. Alternative threshold signature schemes are not conformant.
KEE-2 adds cluster management (key ceremony, signer rotation, quorum
failure handling) that FROST does not specify.

CAEP/SSF [RFC 9672]: KEE-1 P8 (revocation propagation) via CAEP/SSF
applies within each KEE-2 kernel. KEE-2 Section 6 extends revocation
propagation to cross-cluster XPID federation: a revoked GEC cannot
produce valid XPID Federation Certificates.

Emerging AI governance frameworks: KEE-2 D4 Catalog Distribution Protocol is the
technical mechanism by which AI governance frameworks achieve
machine-enforced policy propagation with verifiable effective-
date compliance. The Coordinated Activation protocol maps to the
requirement for simultaneous regulatory activation across all governed
deployments.

APPI (Japan): KEE-2 D3 Cold tier 7-year retention implements APPI
Article 19 audit record retention. Cross-region data residency
constraints in Section 7 implement APPI cross-border transfer controls
for GAR records containing personal data fields.

---

## SECTION 5 — Normative SOOS Cross-References

This draft depends on:
- KEE-1 (draft-sato-soos-kee-00) — all P1-P8 properties remain normative
- CAP-04 (draft-sato-soos-cap-04) — Cedar policy set distributed by D1
- CAP-RRS-02 (draft-sato-soos-cap-rrs-02) — catalog format distributed by D4
- GAR-03 (draft-sato-soos-gar-03) — ALE registry extended by ALE-DIST-01-06
- KIA-03 (draft-sato-soos-kia-03) — FROST signing extended by D2
- AEP-02 (draft-sato-soos-aep-02) — multi-agent sessions supported by D5
- ACD-00 (draft-sato-soos-acd-00) — ACD session inheritance specified in D5
- PEER-00 (draft-sato-soos-peer-00) — XPID model extended in Section 6

No drafts in the current SOOS suite depend on KEE-2 (KEE-2 is a
deployment compliance requirement, not a protocol extension). Drafts
that produce SOOS protocol artifacts (AEP sessions, PEER transactions,
ACD Records) are protocol-level indifferent to whether the underlying
kernel is KEE-1 or KEE-2 compliant.

---

## SECTION 6 — Vienna / Datatracker Status

Draft identifier: draft-sato-soos-dist-00
Session 1 status: Security Considerations (5 attack vectors) + §1-§3
  complete. §4-§9, Appendix A worked example, and Privacy Considerations
  to be authored in Session 2.
Datatracker URL: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-sato-soos-dist/
Target: Post-Vienna submission (KEE-2 is ORDER 18, deferred from
  pre-Vienna sprint per SOOS_UpgradeSprint_v19.md).
Register URL: https://soosproject.ai/drafts/kee2

Open Issues:
- OQ-KEE-03: Session block granularity (one block per session vs. per AEP
  phase; relevant for long-running sessions)
- OQ-KEE-04: Merkle DAG anchor interval normative value
- OQ-KEE-07: Real-time scheduling requirements for FIEA-governed financial
  services (may affect KEE-2 D2 signing latency requirements)
- OQ-KEE-08: Normative performance wall threshold values (W1-W5) —
  current values are provisional pending empirical validation

Japan government track: D4 Catalog Distribution Protocol directly answers
the Fukunaga/Honmaru question on machine-enforced policy propagation.
Cite in Honmaru explainer report alongside CAP-RRS-JP-00.
